name: Aircraft Maintenance Engineer
title: Aircraft Maintenance Engineer (AME)
intro: From Class 12 PCM to a DGCA AME licence: CAR-147 basic training, CAR-66 module exams, practical experience, the licence at 18+, then type ratings.

phases.title: Class 12 PCM
phases.summary: Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics are the standard entry requirement.
points: CAR-147 basic training courses ask for Class 12 with Physics, Chemistry and Mathematics (or a relevant engineering diploma/degree).
Commerce alone is not enough — training organisations and airlines ask for PCM.
AME is a licence, not a degree; some institutes pair training with a degree, but the licence comes from DGCA exams and experience.

phases.title: DGCA-approved CAR-147 training
phases.summary: Join only an organisation on DGCA's approved CAR-147 list.
points: Many institutes advertise "AME courses" — only DGCA-approved CAR-147 organisations count.
Check the approval on dgca.gov.in before paying any fee.
Choose your category early: B1 covers mechanical systems, structures and engines; B2 covers avionics and electrical systems.
phases.tip: Look up the institute on DGCA's list of approved CAR-147 training organisations before you pay.

phases.title: CAR-66 module exams
phases.summary: DGCA subject modules for your category, booked on eGCA.
points: Modules cover maths, physics, electrical, aerodynamics, systems, regulations and more, as set by DGCA.
Exams are applied for and results tracked on the eGCA / Pariksha portals.
The modules you take depend on whether you go for B1 or B2.

phases.title: Practical experience
phases.summary: Hands-on maintenance at an airline or approved maintenance organisation (MRO).
points: DGCA requires practical maintenance experience for your category before you apply for the licence.
Experience is gained at an airline or an approved MRO.
Pay before the licence is modest — the licence is the big step.

phases.title: AME licence, type ratings and growth
phases.summary: Apply to DGCA once modules and experience are complete; then add aircraft types.
points: You must be at least 18 to be issued an AME licence.
A type rating (training on a specific aircraft) lets you certify that type; experience on wide-body or popular types is valued in India and abroad.
Growth path: trainee → licensed AME → certifying engineer → shift/quality manager; work abroad may need licence conversion.
